citation: Yang, Li, Yang, Zhang, Hui and 55 others (Qwen Team) (2025), Qwen3 Technical Report, arXiv 2505.09388v1. Read: abstract page and v1 HTML (Section 4.5, Table 21, small-model evaluation rows)
text_source: Comparable domain: math and code queries for distillation; eval AIME'24, AIME'25, MATH500, LiveCodeBench v5, MMLU-Redux, GPQA-Diamond
feature: Strong-to-weak distillation used to build Qwen3 0.6B-14B: off-policy (teacher responses in think and no-think modes) then on-policy logit distillation; compared with RL
method: From one off-policy-distilled Qwen3-8B checkpoint: RL, or on-policy distillation (student samples, KL to Qwen3-32B or 235B-A22B logits)
outcome: On-policy distillation vs RL: AIME'24 74.4 vs 67.6; AIME'25 65.5 vs 55.5; LiveCodeBench 60.3 vs 52.9; GPQA-D 63.3 vs 61.3; 1,800 vs 17,920 GPU hours; pass@64 90.0 to 93.3 with distillation, unchanged with RL
incremental_to: Off-policy distilled start (AIME'24 55.0); RL from the same start
pit_handling: Not addressed; no overlap check between distillation queries and benchmarks
informs_decision: For a same-tokenizer small student the main lever is on-policy logit distillation, not RL, at about a tenth of the cost; shown at 8B on math and code only

citation: Li, Zhu, Li, Wu, Mammar & Bouvry (2026), Solving Without Stopping: On-Policy Distillation at Small Scale, arXiv 2609.37326v1. Read: abstract page and full v1 text (PDF extracted locally)
text_source: Comparable domain: 13,597 DAPO-Math-17k problems (eval overlaps removed); eval AIME 2026, AMC23, GSM8K-200, GPQA-Diamond
feature: What on-policy distillation transfers to 4B, 1.7B and 0.6B students in thinking vs non-thinking mode; ceilings; answer marking and stopping
method: Teacher Qwen3-8B; one student sample per prompt, clipped per-token reverse-KL advantage, PPO-style, no task reward; 142-212 steps; paired bootstrap intervals
outcome: 0.6B non-thinking p@1 0.048 to 0.328 (teacher 0.595); marked-answer rate +0.633 vs marked-answer accuracy +0.092; distilled p@1 below start p@n in 27/27 cells; thinking mode: 0.6B closure 0.583 to 0.113, no-answer samples 0.328 to 0.579; GPQA-D 0.6B ends at chance (0.234)
incremental_to: Starting student; teacher in the same mode
pit_handling: Training problems overlapping AIME 2024-2026, AMC23 and MATH removed (1,139); AIME 2026 postdates the models
informs_decision: On-policy distillation helps a sub-1B student in non-thinking mode, mostly by teaching it to give an answer; cannot exceed the student's own pass@k; do not distil thinking mode into the 0.8B

citation: Chen, Razin, Narasimhan & Chen (2026), Retaining by Doing: The Role of On-Policy Data in Mitigating Forgetting, ICML 2026 (PMLR 306); arXiv 2510.18874v2. Read: v2 HTML
text_source: Comparable domain: IFEval, MMLU, Countdown as targets; MATH, WildJailbreak, WildGuardTest as non-targets
feature: Forgetting under SFT (70B-teacher answers), Self-SFT (own correct samples), GRPO, REINFORCE, Iterative-SFT, at 1B-8B
method: Llama-3.2-1B, Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen-2.5-1.5B, Qwen-2.5-7B instruct models; 2 epochs; GRPO 5 rollouts; ablations of KL term and advantage estimator
outcome: Non-target drop at 1B/1.5B: SFT 6.2-29.5, Self-SFT 3.0-34.6, GRPO -0.6-1.6 points; at 7B/8B SFT 5.6-38.5 vs GRPO -0.5-3.4; REINFORCE ~ GRPO; KL-forgetting r = 0.52; Iterative-SFT 'mild to no' forgetting (figure only)
incremental_to: Initial instruct model; SFT vs RL at matched epochs
informs_decision: Off-policy teacher SFT (S1 D3) and one-shot self data (D2) both forget; regenerating data from the current student each round is the cheap fix and fits 12 GiB

citation: Wang, Si, Li, Lukasik, Yu, Hsieh, Dhillon & Kumar (2024), Two-stage LLM Fine-tuning with Less Specialization and More Generalization (ProMoT), ICLR 2024; arXiv 2211.00635v3. Read: v3 HTML incl. appendix tables
text_source: RTE, WMT14 En-Fr (fine-tuning); 8 unseen 1-shot tasks (CB, WiC, TriviaQA, web_questions, WMT16 En-De/En-Ro, XSum, WikiLingua)
feature: Format specialisation: single-task fine-tuning overwrites output format on unrelated tasks; soft prompt to absorb format
method: mT5-XXL 13B (checks on T5-XXL, mT5-XL, PaLM 8B); 100-token soft prompt trained, frozen, then model fine-tuned; vs standard FT, multi-task, joint tuning, LoRA stage 1
outcome: After RTE FT ~90% of TriviaQA 1-shot outputs are True/False; TriviaQA 17.58 to 0.15 (ProMoT 17.64); unseen avg 17.52 to 15.43 (FT) vs 20.10 (ProMoT); multi-task FT 20.06, multi-task ProMoT 25.88; target RTE 92.06 vs 92.78; PaLM 8B ProMoT still -3.72
incremental_to: Pretrained model; standard and multi-task fine-tuning
informs_decision: S1's 300/300 boxed numbers on R is format specialisation; first fix is mixing answer formats in training; ProMoT itself is a custom loop untested below 8B

citation: Yang, Pang, Feng, Wang, Chen, Zhu & Liu (2024), Self-Distillation Bridges Distribution Gap in Language Model Fine-Tuning (SDFT), ACL 2024; arXiv 2402.13669v2. Read: v2 HTML incl. Appendix A
text_source: GSM8K, OpenFunctions, MagiCoder/HumanEval, Alpaca, Dolly, LIMA, OpenHermes; AdvBench safety; AlpacaEval
feature: Forgetting caused by the gap between dataset responses and the model's own distribution; model rewrites gold answers before fine-tuning
method: Llama-2-7b-chat (LoRA r=8 and full FT), Llama-3-8B-Instruct; rewrite with gold as reference, keep if final answer matches (math); likelihood loss on rewrites
outcome: Full FT on GSM8K: GSM8K 34.87 vs 35.03; OpenFunctions 5.36 vs 16.07 (seed 19.60); jailbreak-safe 37.31 vs 63.46; win rate 23.04 vs 61.19. LoRA OpenFunctions-trained: target 34.8 vs 36.6, GSM8K 21.5 vs 29.1
incremental_to: Seed model; vanilla fine-tuning on the same data
informs_decision: Cheap fix for forgetting that keeps the target gain under full FT; untested with a rewriter below 7B (open question for a 0.8B)

citation: Agarwal, Vieillard, Zhou, Stanczyk, Ramos, Geist & Bachem (2024), On-Policy Distillation of Language Models: Learning from Self-Generated Mistakes (GKD), ICLR 2024; arXiv 2306.13649v3. Read: abstract page and v3 HTML (most numbers only in figures)
text_source: XSum, WMT14 en-de, GSM8K, FLAN2021 instruction tuning (eval MMLU, BBH)
feature: Generalized KD: student trained on its own samples with teacher token-level feedback; choice of divergence (forward KL, reverse KL, JSD); combination with RL
method: T5-small 77M, base 250M, large 800M students; FLAN-T5-XL / T5-XL teachers; on-policy fraction lambda varied
outcome: On-policy GKD beats supervised KD at all student sizes; at least 25% on-policy data needed, fully on-policy usually best; sampling overhead 1.8-2.2x; T5-small XSum beats PaLM-540B few-shot; reverse KL best for instruction tuning (+2 BBH, +1 MMLU stated)
informs_decision: Sub-1B evidence that on-policy distillation beats off-policy KD; needs shared vocabulary (implied by token-level divergence); method reference for an MLX loop

citation: Gu, Dong, Wei & Huang (2024), MiniLLM: On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models, ICLR 2024; arXiv 2306.08543v6. Read: abstract page and v6 HTML
text_source: Dolly-based instruction data; eval DollyEval, SelfInst, VicunaEval, S-NI, UnNI
feature: Reverse-KL on-policy distillation for generative LMs; exposure bias, calibration
method: Students GPT-2 120M-760M, OPT 1.3B-6.7B, LLaMA-7B; teachers GPT-2-1.5B, OPT-13B, LLaMA-13B; policy-gradient optimisation of reverse KL
outcome: GPT-2 120M, DollyEval GPT-4 score: MiniLLM 44.7 vs SFT 38.6, KD 40.3, SeqKD 41.2 (teacher 58.4); exposure-bias error stops growing after ~150 tokens; LLaMA-7B ECE on SST2 0.099 vs KD 0.191
incremental_to: SFT without KD, word-level KD, sequence-level KD
informs_decision: Reverse-KL on-policy distillation beats off-policy KD at 120M-760M on open generation; supports an on-policy arm over D4's offline top-k KD

citation: Liu, Wu, Zheng, Luo, Yang, Yang, Wang & Yang (2026), Simple-OPD: Demystifying Warm-up for On-policy Distillation, arXiv 2608.06802v1. Read: abstract page and v1 HTML
text_source: Comparable domain: DAPO-Math-17K; ID AMC23, MATH-500, AIME24/25; OOD IFEval, GPQA-D, HumanEval, MMLU-Pro subsets
feature: Warm-up before on-policy distillation: CoT vs no-CoT, teacher vs other-model CoT, correct vs incorrect traces, LoRA vs full SFT
method: Qwen3-1.7B-Base with Qwen3-8B teacher (main); Qwen3-1.7B non-thinking and Qwen3-0.6B thinking with Qwen3-4B teachers; 1 rollout per prompt; no seeds
outcome: Qwen3-0.6B thinking, 4B teacher: ID 42.36 (OPD) vs 43.81 (LoRA warm-up + OPD); Qwen3-1.7B non-thinking: ID 12.81 to 38.34, OOD 40.51 to 47.43; incorrect teacher traces warm up as well as correct (35.2-36.5); full-SFT warm-up 'severely reduces OOD', LoRA does not
incremental_to: Student; vanilla OPD and OPD variants
informs_decision: Closest teacher ratio to S1 (4B into 0.6B); supports LoRA warm-up then OPD; teacher-compatible traces matter more than correctness

citation: DeepSeek-AI (Guo, Yang, Zhang and others) (2025), DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning, Nature 645:633-638; arXiv 2501.12948. Read: abstract page (v2 listing) and v1 HTML Section 4.1
text_source: Comparable domain: math, code, GPQA; 800K R1-curated samples for distillation
feature: Distillation vs large-scale RL for smaller models
method: RL 10K+ steps on Qwen-32B-Base (R1-Zero recipe) vs SFT on R1 outputs; distilled Qwen/Llama 1.5B-70B, SFT only
outcome: Qwen-32B: AIME 47.0 (RL) vs 72.6 (distilled); MATH-500 91.6 vs 94.3; R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B AIME 28.9, MATH-500 83.9 with no RL
incremental_to: QwQ-32B-Preview; RL on the same base
informs_decision: For small models distillation from a strong teacher beats RL at far lower compute; RL left as a later add-on

citation: Chu, Zhai, Yang, Tong, Xie, Schuurmans, Le, Levine & Ma (2025), SFT Memorizes, RL Generalizes: A Comparative Study of Foundation Model Post-training, ICML 2025 (PMLR 267); arXiv 2501.17161v2. Read: abstract page and v2 HTML (first 100K characters)
text_source: Synthetic: GeneralPoints card arithmetic (text and vision), V-IRL navigation; rule and visual variants
feature: Out-of-distribution generalisation of SFT vs outcome-reward RL
method: Llama-3.2-Vision-11B; SFT then RL vs SFT only; verification iterations varied
outcome: OOD rule variants: RL +3.5 (GP-L 11.5 to 15.0) and +11.0 (V-IRL-L), SFT -8.1 (to 3.4) and -79.5 (to 1.3); RL from base fails without SFT (format); RL cannot rescue an overfitted SFT checkpoint
informs_decision: SFT first to fix format, then RL; do not start new arms from S1's collapsed C/K2 checkpoints. Generalisation claim contested by Hou et al. 2026

citation: Hou, Zhang, Cheng, Pan, Li & Yang (2026), Rethinking 'RL Generalizes, SFT Memorizes': The Role of SFT Data, NeurIPS 2026 (per arXiv comments); arXiv 2611.14912v2. Read: abstract page and v2 HTML (first 100K characters)
text_source: Comparable domain: DAPO math; ID AIME24, Minerva, GSM8K, MATH500, OlympiadBench; OOD 12 lm-eval-harness tasks incl. GPQA-D, MMLU-Pro
feature: Whether SFT's poor generalisation comes from its data source and size rather than the objective
method: Qwen2.5-7B (Qwen3-8B-Base in appendix); GRPO 8 rollouts vs SFT on Qwen3-14B or RL-model rollouts, mixes, budgets matched by correct or total rollouts
outcome: MMLU-Pro: RL 45.7, SFT on Qwen3-14B data 1.1, on RL-model data 19.4, 70/30 mix 21.3; base math 42.7 / general 33.8 vs RL 50.9 / 43.8; matching total rollouts (~138K) lets SFT generalise about as well as RL (figure)
informs_decision: SFT data from a larger model can wreck general ability (S1's FinQA drop); data from the student's own neighbourhood and larger budgets narrow the gap to RL

citation: Zeng, Huang, Liu, Liu, He, Ma & He (2025), SimpleRL-Zoo: Investigating and Taming Zero Reinforcement Learning for Open Base Models in the Wild, COLM 2025; arXiv 2503.18892v3. Read: abstract page and v3 HTML
text_source: Comparable domain: GSM8K and MATH training tiers (~8K each); eval GSM8K, MATH500, Minerva, OlympiadBench, AIME24, AMC23
feature: Zero RL (rule reward, no SFT) across 10 base models incl. Qwen2.5-0.5B and 1.5B
method: GRPO-style RL with correctness reward; difficulty matched to model; format-reward and SFT cold-start ablations (7B-24B)
outcome: Qwen2.5-0.5B avg 12.1 to 20.9 (GSM8K 36.7 to 49.5, MATH500 15.8 to 34.4, AIME 0 to 0); 1.5B 18.5 to 36.1; strict format reward slows learning (7-8B); SFT cold start (24B) gives early boost but lower ceiling
informs_decision: RL works at 0.5B on verifiable math but from a low base; avoid rigid format rewards; difficulty must match the student

citation: Shao, Li, Xin, Geng, Wang, Oh, Du, Lambert, Min, Krishna, Tsvetkov, Hajishirzi, Koh & Zettlemoyer (2025), Spurious Rewards: Rethinking Training Signals in RLVR, arXiv 2506.10947v2. Read: abstract page
text_source: Comparable domain: MATH-500
feature: RLVR gains under random or incorrect rewards; model-family dependence
method: GRPO on Qwen2.5-Math, Qwen2.5, Llama3, OLMo2 with true, random and other spurious rewards
outcome: Qwen2.5-Math-7B MATH-500 +21.4 with random rewards vs +29.1 with true rewards; 'code reasoning' 65% to >90%; no such gains for Llama3 or OLMo2
informs_decision: An RL arm on a Qwen student needs a random-reward control; gains may be elicitation not learning

citation: Shenfeld, Damani, Hubotter & Agrawal (2026), Self-Distillation Enables Continual Learning, arXiv 2601.19897v2. Read: abstract page and v2 HTML (first 100K characters)
text_source: Science QA (SciKnowEval Chem L-3), ToolAlpaca, medical (HuatuoGPT-o1 data); knowledge acquisition on 2025 disaster articles
feature: On-policy self-distillation from demonstrations: demonstration-conditioned model as its own teacher
method: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct full FT (3B, 14B size study; Olmo-3-7B-Think); student samples, token-level KL to EMA teacher; vs SFT, SFT+re-invoke, DFT
outcome: New task / prior avg: Science QA SFT 66.2/53.4 vs 70.2/64.5; Tool use 63.2/56.0 vs 70.6/65.4 (base prior 65.5); ~2.5x FLOPs, ~4x wall-clock of SFT; at 3B underperforms SFT, +4 at 7B, +7 at 14B
informs_decision: Self-teacher on-policy methods need in-context ability small models lack; not a 0.8B route; S1 should use the 4B as teacher

citation: Biderman, Portes, Gonzalez Ortiz, Paul, Greengard, Jennings, King, Havens, Chiley, Frankle, Blakeney & Cunningham (2024), LoRA Learns Less and Forgets Less, TMLR (Aug 2024); arXiv 2405.09673v2. Read: abstract page and v2 HTML (first 100K characters)
text_source: Code (Magicoder-Evol-Instruct-110K, StarCoder-Python) and math (MetaMathQA, OpenWebMath); forgetting on HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-Challenge
feature: Learning-forgetting trade-off of LoRA vs full fine-tuning
method: Llama-2-7B; IFT and continued pretraining up to 20B tokens; LoRA ranks 16-256; vs weight decay, dropout
outcome: Math IFT GSM8K: full 0.642, LoRA r=256 0.634, r=16 0.580; retained avg code IFT full 0.414 vs LoRA r=64 0.509, math IFT within 1 point; full FT perturbations rank 10-100x typical LoRA; LoRA lr ~10x full FT
informs_decision: LoRA (high rank, all modules) is an arm to test against S1's full FT for forgetting; gain in retention is domain-dependent

citation: Lin, Y. and 16 others (2024), Mitigating the Alignment Tax of RLHF, EMNLP 2024, pp. 580-606; arXiv 2309.06256v4. Read: v4 HTML (first 100K of 141K characters; many values in figures only)
text_source: HH-RLHF alignment; forgetting on ARC, RACE, PIQA, SQuAD, DROP, WMT14 Fr-En
feature: Forgetting mitigation after alignment: early stopping, L1/L2, LoRA, KD, model averaging, moving average, experience replay
method: OpenLLaMA-3B with RSF (also DPO, PPO); Mistral-7B/Zephyr extension; layer-wise heterogeneous averaging (HMA)
outcome: Model averaging Pareto front 'supersedes nearly all other methods'; beats replay on 2 of 3 benchmarks; alpha 0.2 recommended; HMA Zephyr-7B-beta win rate 8.10 to 9.32, reading 37.47 to 38.93
informs_decision: Weight interpolation of C/K2 with the released 0.8B is a zero-training first test of whether R can be recovered

citation: Hsieh, Li, Yeh, Nakhost, Fujii, Ratner, Krishna, Lee & Pfister (2023), Distilling Step-by-Step!, Findings of ACL 2023; arXiv 2305.02301v2. Read: abstract page and ar5iv full text
text_source: e-SNLI, ANLI, CommonsenseQA, SVAMP; PaLM-540B rationales
feature: Rationales as a separate training task beside the label (multi-task), not generated at test
method: T5 220M, 770M, 11B; loss = label + lambda x rationale with task prefixes; vs fine-tuning, distillation, single-task rationale+label
outcome: 220M at 100% data: ANLI 49.58 vs 43.58 (fine-tuning) vs 43.50 (single-task); 770M with 80% ANLI beats PaLM few-shot CoT; 12.5% e-SNLI beats full fine-tuning
incremental_to: Standard fine-tuning and distillation; few-shot PaLM
informs_decision: Train a short teacher rationale and the answer as two tasks; one combined output can hurt

citation: Fu, Peng, Ou, Sabharwal & Khot (2023), Specializing Smaller Language Models towards Multi-Step Reasoning, ICML 2023 (PMLR 202, pp. 10421-10430); arXiv 2301.12726v1. Read: abstract page and ar5iv full text
text_source: GSM8K CoT from code-davinci-002 (130K kept); eval GSM8K, MultiArith, ASDiv, SVAMP, BIG-Bench Hard
feature: Specialisation trade-off: target reasoning gain vs loss of general ability; data format; checkpoint selection
method: FlanT5 250M, 760M, 3B, 11B (and T5); fine-tune on teacher CoT; distribution vs sample matching
outcome: GSM8K +8.9 to +13.3; BBH-CoT 25.9-41.8 to 0.0-0.3; BBH-AO 24.2-47.4 to 3.1-19.6; in-context-format data keeps zero-shot ability, not vice versa; selecting on GSM8K dev does not give best OOD checkpoint
informs_decision: Narrowing is the expected price of single-task distillation below 11B; mix formats and select checkpoints on held-out families

citation: Zhu, Qi, Zhang, Long, Lin & Zhou (2024), PaD: Program-aided Distillation Can Teach Small Models Reasoning Better than Chain-of-thought Fine-tuning, NAACL 2024; arXiv 2305.13888v2. Read: abstract page and v2 HTML (first 100K characters)
text_source: Synthetic GSM8K programs from gpt-3.5-turbo (5.9K; 45.9K augmented); eval GSM8K, ASDiv, SVAMP, MultiArith, BBH
feature: Executable programs instead of free-text CoT as distillation targets; error checking; self-refinement
method: CodeT5 60M, 220M, 770M; program filtering by execution; step-wise verified beam search
outcome: 770M GSM8K PaD 44.9 vs fine-tune 7.5; same teacher and similar data: 21.7 (PaD) vs 13.46 (CoT); BBH falls 12.0/10.2/28.1 to 1.7/2.0/1.9
informs_decision: Executable steps beat free text for tiny students (S1's calculator already covers this); specialisation again erases general ability

citation: Wen, Huang, Li, Li, Zhong, Xu, Yuan, Huang & Xu (2025), Reasoning Scaffolding: Distilling the Flow of Thought from LLMs, arXiv 2509.23619v2. Read: abstract page and v2 HTML
text_source: DeepSeek-R1 traces; eval StrategyQA, CommonsenseQA, TruthfulQA, GSM8K, MATH-500
feature: Distilling a structured scaffold (7 discourse-level step signals) rather than imitating free text
method: Qwen2.5-Instruct 0.5B, 7B, 14B, LoRA; signals by keyword plus GPT-4.1 labelling; multi-task loss (predict signal, then step) with signal embedding added to hidden state
outcome: 0.5B pass@1 5-task mean about 0.40 (original), 0.49 (CoT SFT), 0.61 (scaffold), e.g. GSM8K 0.379/0.394/0.488; tokens 2.9-6.9x CoT SFT; random signals worse than gold at 0.5B
informs_decision: Structured step labels can help a 0.5B more than free-text CoT, but need labelling and a model change; later option after short-rationale multi-task SFT
